title: Earlier health-insurance noncoverage is followed by lower political contact and action in a CCES panel
source_unit: 9,499 respondents in the retained 2010–2012–2014 Cooperative Congressional Election Study panel with valid 2012 health-insurance status; same-panel descriptive follow-up to 2014 political outcomes

observations.period: 2012 health-insurance status followed by 2014 political outcomes

denominator.unit: panel respondents with valid 2012 health-insurance noncoverage item and supplied panel weight; Congress approval valid rows vary

no_insurance_screen.value: 912 no insurance (15.49% weighted); 8,587 with some insurance
no_insurance_screen.unit: 2012 healthins_6 status; unweighted group counts and weighted population share

congress_approval_favorable.value: 11.51% after 2012 no insurance versus 10.23% among insured respondents
congress_approval_favorable.unit: weighted share approving Congress somewhat or strongly in 2014; valid n=909 and 8,543

congress_approval_unfavorable.value: 74.77% after 2012 no insurance versus 83.07% among insured respondents
congress_approval_unfavorable.unit: weighted share disapproving Congress somewhat or strongly in 2014; valid n=909 and 8,543

any_congress_contact.value: 31.75% after 2012 no insurance versus 40.29% among insured respondents
any_congress_contact.unit: weighted share reporting any 2014 congressional contact route among visited/called/written/received/public-event/other fields

any_local_political_action.value: 21.81% after 2012 no insurance versus 32.48% among insured respondents
any_local_political_action.unit: weighted share reporting any 2014 local political meeting, political sign, campaign work, or political donation

observations.method: Classify 2012 healthins_6=1 as no insurance and =2 as some form of insurance in the retained panel; apply the supplied panel weight to 2014 outcome shares. Favorable Congress approval is codes 1–2 and unfavorable approval codes 3–4. Any congressional contact is any affirmative CC14_360x_2 through CC14_360x_8; any local political action is any affirmative CC14_417a_1 through CC14_417a_4.
observations.uncertainty: Health-insurance status is a survey status, not a dated coverage loss, bill, denial, care need, or causal exposure. The panel is selected and retained; the supplied weight's representativeness for this derived transition is not independently re-established. Prior political identity, health, income, employment, age, policy knowledge, local conditions, and other shocks remain. No replicate-weight or causal uncertainty estimate is claimed.
observations.subgroup: 2012 no-insurance versus insured respondents in the retained three-wave panel; 2014 Congress-approval outcomes have separate valid-answer universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Noncoverage may indicate age, employment, health, income, or other resource differences that also shape time and ability to participate. Lower contact and action do not prove withdrawal, distrust, or a health-policy mechanism; the near-similar favorable-approval shares show that action and institutional judgment can diverge.

related_sources.claim: The Cooperative Election Study identifies the 2010–2014 panel as a three-wave panel with 9,500 respondents re-interviewed in 2014.
The retained panel audit documents the local extract, field definitions, weight, and related work-to-politics screen.

boundary: This is a same-panel descriptive follow-up from 2012 health-insurance status to 2014 institutional approval, congressional contact, and local political action. It does not establish a dated coverage shock, causal health-cost effect, trust change, political withdrawal, remedy, recovery, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Retained local 9,500-row CCES panel Stata extract; raw panel file remains outside the repository
